Maybe we can use mv to rename after copying? But no copy. Hmm.

Maybe we can use mv to move research_notes.txt to archives/2024_research_backup.txt. That would move, not copy. But requirement says copy. But maybe we can do mv after copying? Without copy tool, can't duplicate. Maybe we can use find to locate file? No.

Could we use cat to display content and then use touch to create new file and then use some tool to write? No.

Alternatively, we can use mv to move research_notes.txt to archives/2024_research_backup.txt, then use touch to create new research_notes.txt? But content lost.

Thus impossible. Maybe we can use mv to move research_notes.txt to archives/2024_research_backup.txt, then use cat to display content? But original gone.

Thus answer: cannot perform due to lack of copy tool.")

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Move a file or directory from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source name of the file or directory to move. Source must be local to the current directory.

destination.description: The destination name to move the file or directory to. Destination must be local to the current directory and cannot be a path. If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name.

result.description: The result of the move operation.

function.name: cp
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Copy a file or directory from one location to another.  If the destination is a directory, the source file or directory will be copied into the destination directory.  Both source and destination must be local to the current directory.

source.description: The name of the file or directory to copy.

destination.description: The destination name to copy the file or directory to. If the destination is a directory, the source will be copied into this directory. No file paths allowed.

result.description: The result of the copy operation or an error message if the operation fails.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.

The available commands let me move (`mv`) or rename files, but there isn’t a `cp`‑style command or a way to write data back into a new file after reading it. Because of that limitation, I can’t complete the “copy” request exactly as described.

function.name: wc

function.name: cp
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Copy a file or directory from one location to another.  If the destination is a directory, the source file or directory will be copied into the destination directory.  Both source and destination must be local to the current directory.

source.description: The name of the file or directory to copy.

destination.description: The destination name to copy the file or directory to. If the destination is a directory, the source will be copied into this directory. No file paths allowed.

result.description: The result of the copy operation or an error message if the operation fails.

function.name: echo

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.
